title: Backlog Slimming — Sanity Check & Prioritization (July 2026)
body:
Context and purpose:
This doc captures the grooming session notes for a backlog slimming exercise focused on the Console & Rollouts area. Goal is to reduce the active backlog by ~30% ahead of Sprint 22 planning and to ensure remaining items have clear outcomes, owners, and success criteria. This is an operational sanity-check rather than a full reprioritization — we want quick deciders, fast wins, and clear candidates for deferral or rewrite.

Goals for this session:
- Identify items to move to a short-term 'must ship' list (<= 6 items) for the next 2 sprints.
- Mark items suitable for deferral to the quarter backlog (>= 12 week horizon).
- Convert ambiguous tickets into actionably scoped tasks or spin them out as spike tickets.
- Call out UX wireframes that need revision before dev picks them up.

Participants and roles:
- Ava (owner / facilitator) — leads the session, aligns on success criteria.
- Ravi (PM) — clarifies product intent and customer impact.
- Lina (UX) — flags wireframe gaps and acceptance criteria.
- Marco (SRE) — feasibility/cost signals for routing and infra changes.
- Sofia (SWE) — rough dev effort estimates.
- Jonah (Solutions Eng) — customer impact / customer ask validation.

Prioritization rubric used (quick scoring):
- Customer criticality (0–3): Is this blocking customers or enterprise deals?
- Operational risk (0–2): Does it reduce toil or incident likelihood?
- Developer unblocker (0–2): Unblocks multiple teams/projects?
- Effort (0–3, inverse): Lower score for high effort.
- UX clarity (-1 if wireframe missing / ambiguous).
We scored each candidate ticket against this rubric; items with total >=5 were flagged high-priority.

Shortlist (must-consider for next 2 sprints):
1) RW-1254: "Rollout canary config stops at 50%" — Score 7. Reason: Enterprise customers experiencing flaky rollouts; short mitigation available (config UI + brief server guardrail). Outcome: ship canary guardrail + monitoring alert. Owner: Ravi. Dev estimate: 3d. Wireframe: small config modal tweak (Lina to update).
2) RW-1349: "Route by cost tier policy UI" — Score 6. Reason: Important for Dedicated customers; medium effort but high commercial value. Outcome: initial MVP with toggles and clear help text. Owner: Marco. Dev estimate: 5d but split into backend and UI tasks. Wireframe: exists but needs copy edits.
3) RW-1412 (new spike): "KV cache visibility for routes" — Score 5. Reason: SRE and customers asking for visibility into cache hit rates. Create spike to define metrics and storage cost. Owner: Marco. Dev estimate: spike 2d.
4) UX-2137: "Shortcut flow for model pinning" — Score 6. Reason: Common support ask; quick nav addition could reduce support tickets. Owner: Lina. Dev estimate: 2d front-end change + 1d QA. Wireframe: draft ready, Lina to iterate.
5) DOC-77: "Console onboarding checklist for Private deployments" — Score 5. Reason: Reduces onboarding time for sales/SEs; doc-first deliverable. Owner: Jonah. Dev estimate: 1d to finalize.

Candidates to defer (quarter backlog):
- RW-1120: Multi-tenant billing export rewrite — high effort, low immediate ROI; defer.
- UX-1850: Full redesign of rollout history page — large scope and many unanswered UX questions; convert to discovery project (Q4).
- INF-300: Autoscale policy language overhaul — infra-only heavy lift, schedule for Dedicated roadmap window.

Tickets that need rewriting / spikes:
- RW-1290: "Console slow when switching models" — vague. Action: create perf spike to identify root cause, capture reproduction steps (Sofia + Marco).
- RW-1388: "Batch size UI default mismatch" — unclear acceptance criteria. Action: PM to specify desired behavior and add e2e check.

Wireframe notes (UX quick wins):
- Topbar: add compact model switcher suggestion (Lina). Keep pattern consistent with hosted API dashboard.
- Canary modal: show timeline + rollback action more prominently; small copy change to explain percentage semantics.
- Cost-tier routing panel: provide inline examples and an 'opt-in preview' sandbox so customers can simulate traffic.
- Accessibility: ensure all modals have focus traps and descriptive aria labels (action item for Lina).

Sprint allocation proposal (Sprint 22 / Sprint 23):
Sprint 22 (2 weeks): RW-1254 (canary guardrail), UX-2137 (model pinning shortcut), DOC-77.
Sprint 23: RW-1349 (route by cost tier MVP backend + UI split), RW-1412 spike + follow-up plan.
Rationale: balance customer-facing fixes with a backend/infra item. Keep one low-effort doc/task per sprint to ensure velocity.

Acceptance criteria examples (to include in each ticket before dev start):
- RW-1254: rollout canary retains percent + metadata after server restart; automated smoke test replicates 50% routing and triggers rollback policy.
- UX-2137: shortcut accessible via keyboard; reduces clicks by >=2 from current flow.
- RW-1349: routing toggle persists and is logged in audit trail; sample rule tested with synthetic traffic.

Open questions and risks:
- Do we have capacity for RW-1349 backend work given Dedicated infra windows? (Marco to confirm by 2026-07-14).
- RW-1254 rollback semantics may need coordination with the runtime team for guardrail enforcement — potential scope creep.
- Dependencies on analytics ingestion for RW-1412 may push spike further if infra quotas are hit.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Lina: update canary modal wireframe + topbar sketch (due 2026-07-14).
- Marco: confirm infra availability for RW-1349 (due 2026-07-14).
- Ravi: break RW-1254 into backend guardrail ticket and UI modal ticket; set PR checklist (due 2026-07-13).
- Sofia: run perf reproduction steps for RW-1290 and create perf spike ticket (due 2026-07-16).
- Jonah: finalize onboarding checklist draft and share with SEs (due 2026-07-15).

Quick grooming heuristics we applied (for future sessions):
- If a ticket has sat >90 days with no updates, either close or rewrite into a spike.
- Anything with >=2 external customer asks moves to a 'customer-impact' lane and gets higher attention.
- Small UI copy + accessibility fixes get grouped into a weekly 'frontline fixes' batch (1d capacity).

Notes for follow-up meeting (2026-07-16):
- Review Lina's wireframe updates and confirm acceptance criteria.
- Finalize Sprint 22 sprint plan in Jira board (Ravi to create slice tickets).
- Validate resource commitments from infra and SRE (Marco & Sofia).

Appendix: quick links and rough estimates used during scoring:
- Historical support tickets referencing rollouts: https://zendesk.redwood.ai/tickets?query=rollout
- Metric: median rollout failure impact = 2.4 incidents/month (SRE dashboard)
- Average front-end task estimate = 2.2d; backend = 3.7d; spike = 1.5d

Unresolved: several small backlog items were ambiguous and we left a short "shelf" list (ownerless) to be re-evaluated in 30 days. We recommend a recurring 60-minute 'backlog slimming' slot every 4 weeks to keep the console backlog healthy.

End notes: This is intentionally pragmatic — pick a few high-impact items, defer the rest, and tighten tickets so devs can start without long discovery loops.
